AUDIT QUESTION: TASK: audit batch 119 of the Protocol Pulse video pipeline (Python). You are reviewing a diff. Only state what you can verify from the diff and the cited lines. If uncertain, say so. Do not guess.

CONTEXT. RULING 142 (3) (Nov 17): a post_live YouTube stream (ended live, still processing; DASH formats only) cannot be cut by yt-dlp --download-sections; the pipeline fetches the WHOLE stream once (select_passages._post_live_window, cached per video) and cuts the window locally, writing <out>.post_live.json; pinned.acquire then runs a HARD clock guard on such a source (pinned.py:286-288 post_live_offset: the decode's word times must match the transcript's, else PinError). Today that route is entered in ONE place only: select_passages._download_window (select_passages.py:~95-135, unchanged) calls _post_live_window when the section download COMPLETES with a file that has no media. FAILURE TONIGHT: Bitcoin Magazine U7X6kReXets (post_live, 7134 s) did not complete: the section download ran past its 120 s timeout twice (19:03, 19:48 ET); _download_window printed "download timeout" and returned None before the whole-stream route was tried, so the lock pre-check had no window and the render would fail the same way (pinned.acquire raises "source download failed"). select_passages.py and pinned.py are hashed into the lock pre-check's DECODER sha (a change there needs a lockstep with another session), so they are not touched.

WHAT THE DIFF DOES:
1. New pipeline/post_live_prefetch.py: prefetch(video_id, start, end, run_dir) calls _download_window first (unchanged behaviour when it returns a window). Only when it returns nothing AND yt-dlp reports live_status == "post_live" does it call _post_live_window(video_id, dl_start, end + 15, run_dir/sources/<id>.mp4, cookies) with dl_start = round(max(0, start - 15)), the exact start _download_window uses (pad 15 s), and return (path, dl_start). Any other status: None, as before.
2. run_fresh.stage_pinned calls prefetch_post_live(run, pin_path) before pinned.prepare: for each YouTube video of the pin, prefetch over [min start, max end] of its segments (pinned.acquire's own window, pinned.py:277). Then pinned.acquire's own _download_window call is a cache hit on that file (select_passages: `if os.path.exists(out_path) and os.path.getsize(out_path) > 100_000: return out_path, dl_start`) and, the .post_live.json being there, the HARD clock guard runs.
3. lock_precheck.prefetch (runs before the GPU lease) calls post_live_prefetch.prefetch instead of _download_window directly, into the same work_dir.

CHECK, AND ANSWER EACH:
Q1. Is the window cut through this new entry the same window, with the same start offset, that _download_window and pinned.acquire use (so the clock guard and the cut tables read it correctly)?
Q2. Can this route admit a source the old route would have refused: a non-post_live video, a failed or partial whole-stream download, a file without media, a window without the .post_live.json record (which would skip the clock guard)?
Q3. Failure handling: an unreadable pin, a yt-dlp probe that fails or hangs, _post_live_window returning False: does anything crash the stage or the pre-check, or hang it longer than the existing timeouts?
Q4. Any other defect.

+    """yt-dlp's live_status for the video (post_live, was_live, not_live ...), or None when it cannot be read."""

+        cmd += ["--cookies", COOKIES]
+    try:
+        r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
+        d = json.loads(r.stdout or "{}")

+        return None
+    return d.get("live_status") if isinstance(d, dict) else None
+
+
+def prefetch(video_id, start_s, end_s, run_dir, log=print):
+    """The window pinned.acquire will ask for: -> (path, dl_start) as _download_window returns it, or None."""
+    from select_passages import _download_window, _post_live_window
+    res = _download_window(video_id, start_s, end_s, run_dir)

+    status = live_status(video_id)
+    if status != "post_live":
+        log(f"  {video_id}: the window did not download (live_status {status}): no whole-stream route")
+        return None
+    out = os.path.join(run_dir, "sources", f"{video_id}.mp4")
+    dl_start = float(round(max(0, start_s - PAD_S)))
+    log(f"  {video_id}: post_live, the window did not download: cutting it from the whole stream (ruling 142 (3))")
+    if _post_live_window(video_id, dl_start, end_s + PAD_S, out, COOKIES if os.path.exists(COOKIES) else None):
+        return out, dl_start
+    log(f"  {video_id}: the whole-stream route gave no media")
+    return None
